claims.body: Retail CFD spreads widen sharply into and through scheduled releases, and again at the daily rollover. On XAUUSD the widening is a material multiple of the normal spread.
claims.why_it_matters: A stop that costs 3% of your risk in normal conditions can cost 25% through a release. Check the live spread before entering, not the average.
sources: broker behaviour, generic to retail CFD venues

claims.body: Headline macro prints are frequently revised, and the initial market reaction often reverses within hours once the detail is read.
claims.why_it_matters: The first candle after a release is the least informative one of the day. Trading the reaction is a different skill from trading the data.

claims.body: What matters is the surprise against expectations, not the absolute number. A weak print that is less weak than feared is bullish.
claims.why_it_matters: Check OIS-implied pricing before the event to know what is already in the price.

claims.body: As of late August 2026, CME FedWatch pricing implied roughly 40% odds of a September HIKE and 60% unchanged — not a cut. Sources conflicted: some commentary still quoted an 85% cut probability. Treat as contested.
claims.why_it_matters: Much gold commentary assumes a cut is coming. If the hawkish pricing is right, the rate leg of the gold bull case points the wrong way. Verify against current FedWatch before relying on it — this claim decays fast.
